h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר ט׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Tes

p: הָרִאשׁוֹנִים קוֹרִין לְשַׁבָּת זוֹ שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל,
The early authorities call this Shabbos "Shabbos HaGadol,"
וּלְשׁוֹן "גָּדוֹל" מָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
and we find the term "Gadol" (Great) in the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים קי"ח.)
(Pesachim 118a)
בְּהַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל:
regarding the Great Hallel:
וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל?
"And why is it called the Great Hallel?
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
Because the Holy One, blessed is He, sits in the heights of the universe
וּמְחַלֵּק מְזוֹנוֹת לְכָל בְּרִיָּה.
and distributes sustenance to every creature."
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י:
And Rashi explained:
דִּכְתִיב:
"As it is written:
הוֹדוּ לְאֵל הַשָּׁמָיִם... נֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר,
'Give thanks to the God of Heaven... Who gives bread to all flesh,'
וְהַיְינוּ דָּבָר גָּדוֹל,
and this is a great thing,"
עַד כָּאן.
(up to here).
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין:
Now one must understand:
דְּהָא פָּסוּק הוֹדוּ לְאֵל הַשָּׁמָיִם נִכְתַּב אַחַר הַפָּסוּק נֹתֵן לֶחֶם וְגוֹמֵר;
surely the verse "Give thanks to the God of Heaven" is written after the verse "Who gives bread, etc.";
גַּם מָה הַלָּשׁוֹן "יוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם"?
also, what is the meaning of the expression "sits in the heights of the universe"?
הֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם, כִּלְשׁוֹן אֵל הַשָּׁמָיִם!
It should have said that He sits in Heaven, matching the phrasing "God of Heaven"!
אַךְ מָצִינוּ לָשׁוֹן זֶה בַּגְּמָרָא
However, we find this expression in the Gemara
(מְנָחוֹת כ"ט:):
(Menachos 29b):
חָטְרֵי לְהוּ לְגַגּוֹ דְּחֵי"ת
"They crowned the roof of the letter Ches"
כְּלוֹמַר: חַי הוּא בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
meaning: He is the Living One in the heights of the universe.
וְשָׁם הַמְכוּוָן הוּא עַתִּיקָא שֶׁנִּקְרָא רוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
And there the reference is to Atika, which is called "the heights of the universe,"
שֶׁכֵּן לָשׁוֹן "רָם" וְ"גָּדוֹל" לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסַת הַשָּׂגַת בְּנֵי אָדָם.
for the terms "lofty" and "great" denote that which is beyond human grasp and comprehension.
וְכֵן הַמְכוּוָן כָּאן:
And so too is the intent here:
יוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
"sits in the heights of the universe"
הַיְינוּ עַתִּיקָא,
refers to Atika,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
and is based on what they said
(מוֹעֵד קָטָן כ"ח.):
(Moed Katan 28a):
חַיֵּי בְּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי לָאו בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָין אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא.
"Life, children, and sustenance do not depend on merit, rather the matter depends on mazal (supernal flow)."
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' ע"ט:)
מְפָרֵשׁ:
it explains:
מַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא עַתִּיקָא.
"The holy mazal is Atika."
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(שְׁמוּאֵל א' א', י'):
(I Shmuel 1:10):
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל חַנָּה עַל ה'
"And she prayed upon (al) Hashem"
"עַל" דַּיְיקָא, דְּהָא בְּנִין בְּמַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא תַּלְיָין וְכוּלֵּי;
specifically "upon" (above), for children depend on the holy mazal, etc.;
הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה' יְהָבְךָ
"Cast upon (al) Hashem your burden"
"עַל" דַּיְיקָא, דְּהָא מְזוֹנֵי בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָין.
specifically "upon" (above), for sustenance depends on mazal.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 118a — "Why is it called the Great Hallel? Rabbi Yochanan said: Because the Holy One, blessed is He, sits in the heights of the world and distributes sustenance to every creature." Rashbam: as it is written, "Give thanks to the God of heaven... Who gives bread to all flesh" (Tehillim 136:25-26), and that is a great thing.

Rashi: the roof of the Ches is made with a raised point above, meaning that the Holy One, blessed is He, Who lives forever, dwells in the heights of the world.

inlineHeadings.text: Why the Great Hallel is called great
Crowning the roof of the Ches: Atika
Life, children and sustenance depend on mazal

p: וְהַיְינוּ לְמַעְלָה מִשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ"ה,
And this means above the Name Havayah,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל תֵּשַׁע הַמִּדּוֹת:
which indicates the nine attributes:
י' חָכְמָה, ה' בִּינָה, ו' תִּפְאֶרֶת כָּלוּל שִׁית סְפִירָאָן, ה' מַלְכוּת
Yud is Chochmah, Hei is Binah, Vav is Tiferes encompassing six Sefiros, and Hei is Malchus
(זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג' רנ"ח סוֹף ע"א),
(holy Zohar, Vol. 3, 258, end of amud a),
וְקוֹצָא דְּיוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָּא רְמִיזָא לְאֵין, כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and the upper tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness), Kesser Elyon
(ibid. 65b, 10b).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ "עַל" דַּיְיקָא
And this is why they said specifically "upon" (above)
עַל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה.
above the Name Havayah.
וְה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים,
And Hashem, may He be blessed, is the root of life,
וְזֶה "חַי הוּא בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם",
and this is "He is the Living One in the heights of the universe,"
וְכֵן כָּאן: יוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וּמְחַלֵּק מְזוֹנוֹת לְכָל בְּרִיָּה.
and similarly here: "sits in the heights of the universe and distributes sustenance to every creature."
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין צָרִיךְ רְאָיָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם,
And in truth, no proof is needed that the Holy One, blessed is He, sits in Heaven,
שֶׁכָּל הַתּוֹרָה מָלֵא מִזֶּה: יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם וְכַדּוֹמֶה;
for the entire Torah is full of this—"He who sits in Heaven" and the like;
רַק שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ הֵם הָעוֹלָם, וְהֵם רוֹמְזִים לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ,
rather, Heaven and Earth are the universe, and they allude to the Holy One, blessed is He, and His Shechinah,
שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה וְשֵׁם אֲדֹנָי,
the Name Havayah and the Name Adonai,
וְרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם עַתִּיקָא עַל הֲוָיָ"ה, קוֹצָא דְּיוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָּא.
and "the heights of the universe" is Atika above Havayah, the upper tip of the Yud.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה נִקְרָא "גָּדוֹל",
And for this reason it is called "Great,"
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר עַד לְמַעְלָה מֵהַתְּפִיסָה,
which indicates without measure, reaching beyond comprehension,
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
similar to what they said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נ"ג, י'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 53:10):
מִשְׁתֶּה גָּדוֹל
"A great feast"
גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים הָיָה שָׁם;
"The Great One of the worlds was there";
גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים — רוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
"the Great One of the worlds" is "the heights of the universe."
אַךְ מָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא בְּרָכוֹת
Yet we find in the Gemara, Berachos
כָּל הָאוֹמֵר תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בַּיּוֹם וְכוּלֵּי...
"Whoever recites 'Tehillah L'David' (Ashrei) three times a day, etc....
אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ "פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ".
Rather, because it contains the verse 'You open Your hand.'
נֵימָא הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ "נֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר"!
Let one recite the Great Hallel, in which it is written 'Who gives bread to all flesh'!
אֶלָּא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי.
Rather, because [Tehillah L'David] has two qualities."
וּלְפִי הָאָמוּר, שֶׁעַל זֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ רְאָיָה שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם דִּמְזוֹנֵי בְּמַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא תַּלְיָין,
And according to what was just said—that no proof is needed that He sits in the heights of the universe since sustenance depends on the holy mazal
אִם כֵּן לָמָּה לֹא נִקְרָא תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל?
if so, why is Tehillah L'David not called the Great Hallel?
וְאַדְּרַבָּה יוֹתֵר יִתָּכֵן לִקְרוֹת הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל לִתְהִלָּה לְדָוִד עַל שֵׁם הַפָּסוּק:
On the contrary, it would be even more fitting to call Tehillah L'David the Great Hallel on account of the verse:
פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ וּמַשְׂבִּיעַ לְכָל חַי רָצוֹן,
"You open Your hand and satisfy the desire (ratzon) of every living thing,"
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
for it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ס"ב.):
מַאי רָצוֹן?
"What is 'ratzon'?
הַהוּא רָצוֹן דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא.
That is the Will that is found from Atika Kadisha."
וְהַמַּהַרְשָׁ"א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And the Maharsha, of blessed memory
(בִּפְסָחִים)
(in Pesachim)
עָמַד עַל זֶה:
addressed this question:
לָמָּה לֹא קָרְאוּ תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי?
why did they not call Tehillah L'David the Great Hallel, since it has both qualities?
וְתֵירֵץ דִּבְהוֹדוּ טְפֵי מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּפָּסוּק שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר.
And he answered that in "Hodu" it is more explicitly stated in the verse that He gives bread to all flesh.
וְלֹא נִתְבָּאֵר בִּדְבָרָיו הַחִילּוּק בֵּין "לְכָל בָּשָׂר" אוֹ "לְכָל חַי".
Yet he did not explain in his words the distinction between "to all flesh" and "to every living thing."
אַךְ יִתָּכֵן דִּבְתְהִלָּה לְדָוִד כְּתִיב:
However, it may be that in Tehillah L'David it is written:
וּמַשְׂבִּיעַ לְכָל חַי רָצוֹן,
"and satisfies every living thing with desire/contentment,"
וְיָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת שֶׁנּוֹתֵן רָצוֹן בְּהָאָדָם שֶׁיִּשְׂמַח בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְיַסְפִּיק לוֹ,
which could mean that He places contentment within a person so that he rejoices in his portion and it suffices for him,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
along the lines of what they said
(בְּרָכוֹת כ':):
(Berachos 20b):
כְּתִיב בַּתּוֹרָה: וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ,
"It is written in the Torah: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied,'
וְהֵם מְדַקְדְּקִין עַל עַצְמָם עַד כְּזַיִת וְעַד כְּבֵיצָה.
yet they are strict with themselves even down to an olive's bulk or an egg's bulk."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כָּאן דִּכְתִיב:
Not so here, where it is written:
נֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר
"Who gives bread to all flesh"
וְהַיְינוּ מְזוֹנֵי מַמָּשׁ,
which means actual physical sustenance,
וּמְזוֹנֵי בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָין, דְּהוּא עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא וְנִקְרָא גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים,
and sustenance depends on mazal, which is Atika Kadisha and is called "the Great One of the worlds,"
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה נִקְרָא הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל.
and for this reason it is called the Great Hallel.
וְאֶפְשָׁר לְיַשֵּׁב בְּכַוָּונַת רַשִׁ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה דְּמַיְיתֵי הַכָּתוּב דְּהוֹדוּ לְאֵל הַשָּׁמָיִם,
And it is also possible to reconcile the intent of Rashi, of blessed memory, in citing the verse "Give thanks to the God of Heaven,"
שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא "גָּדוֹל" שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם:
that on account of this it is called "Great," because He sits in the heights of the universe:
דְּשֵׁם אֵל הוּא שֵׁם שֶׁל חֶסֶד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
for the Name Keil is a Name of Chessed, as brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' ס"ה.):
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 65a):
אֵל נְהִירוּ דְּחָכְמְתָא וְאִיקְרֵי חֶסֶד,
"Keil is the illumination of Chochmah and is called Chessed,"
וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַחֶסֶד בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר עַד עַתִּיקָא
and the expansion of Chessed reaches without measure up to Atika
(וְכֵן כָּתַב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם י"א:):
(and so wrote the holy Zohar, ibid. 11b:
רְבִיעָאָה אֵל גָּדוֹל, וְהָא אִיתְּמַר וְדָא גְּדוּלָּה),
"The fourth is Keil Gadol, and it has been taught that this is Gedulah"),
וּלְךָ ה' הַגְּדֻלָּה הַיְינוּ חֶסֶד.
and "Yours, Hashem, is the greatness (Gedulah)" means Chessed.
וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּן רַשִׁ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה לְדַקְדֵּק מִתֵּיבַת "הַשָּׁמָיִם", רַק מִשֵּׁם "אֵל",
Thus Rashi, of blessed memory, did not intend to derive his point from the word "Heaven," rather from the Name "Keil,"
וְהַמְכוּוָן שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא יוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא עַתִּיקָא גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים.
meaning that on account of this He is called "sitting in the heights of the universe," which is Atika, the Great One of the worlds.
וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: ה' רֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר
And some say [the Great Hallel is] "Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack"
(פְּסָחִים שָׁם),
(Pesachim, ibid.),
וּמְפָרְשִׁים שֶׁזֶּה הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עַל שֵׁם הַמָּזוֹן.
and they explain that this is the Great Hallel recited on account of sustenance.
וְקָשֶׁה לְפִי זֶה:
Yet according to this, there is a difficulty:
מְנָא לֵיהּ לְתַנָּא דְּבָרַיְיתָא לְמִיעְבַּד פְּלוּגְתָּא בֵּין רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים?
from where did the Tanna of the Baraisa know to establish a dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and the "some say"?
הָא רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן סְתָמָא קָאָמַר: וְאוֹמֵר הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל,
After all, Rabbi Tarfon stated without specification, "And one recites the Great Hallel,"
וְדִלְמָא גַּם כֵּן נִתְכַּוֵּן עַל מִזְמוֹר ה' רֹעִי וְגוֹמֵר?!
so perhaps he too intended the psalm "Hashem is my shepherd, etc."?!
אַךְ נִרְאֶה דְּהַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ,
Rather, it appears that according to everyone, the Great Hallel is the twenty-six verses of "Ki l'olam chasdo" (Psalm 136),
רַק הַיֵּשׁ אוֹמְרִים סְבִירָא לֵיהּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹמַר גַּם כֵּן אַחַר עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ מִזְמוֹר ה' רֹעִי וְגוֹמֵר.
only the "some say" hold that one must also recite after the twenty-six "Ki l'olam chasdo" verses the psalm "Hashem is my shepherd, etc."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ פְּלִיגִי מֵהֵיכָן הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל,
And afterward they dispute where the Great Hallel begins
גַּם כֵּן לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא:
also according to everyone's understanding [of what the Great Hallel is]:
מָר אָמַר עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ,
one master says the twenty-six verses of "Ki l'olam chasdo,"
וּמָר אָמַר מִשִּׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת,
and one master says from "Shir HaMa'alos" (Psalm 134),
וְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מִ"כִּי יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ יָהּ",
and Rav Acha bar Yaakov says from "For Yaakov did Kah choose for Himself" (Psalm 135:4)
וּבְוַדַּאי הַמְכוּוָן מִתְּחִילַּת הַמִּזְמוֹר: הַלְלוּיָהּ הַלְלוּ אֶת שֵׁם ה' וְגוֹמֵר.
and certainly his intent is from the beginning of that psalm, "Halleluyah, praise the Name of Hashem, etc."
וְלָמָּה נָקַט רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב דַּיְיקָא פָּסוּק זֶה?
Then why did Rav Acha bar Yaakov cite specifically this verse?
וְהוּא אֲשֶׁר דִּיבַּרְנוּ, שֶׁנִּקְרָא "גָּדוֹל" עַל שֵׁם עַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים חַי בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
It is just as we have spoken: that it is called "Great" after Atika, which is the Great One of the worlds, living in the heights of the universe,
וּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
and he holds it is named after what is said
(תְּהִלִּים קל"ה, ד'):
(Tehillim 135:4):
כִּי יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ יָהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְגֻלָּתוֹ וְגוֹמֵר.
"For Yaakov did Kah choose for Himself, Israel as His treasured possession (segulah), etc."
וּסְגוּלָּה פֵּירֵשׁ הַיְּהוּדִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
And "segulah" was explained by the Holy Yehudi, may the memory of the righteous and holy be for a blessing,
שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ דָּבָר סְגוּלִּי בְּלִי טַעַם,
to be like a medicinal/supernatural remedy (segulah) that works without rational explanation;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר
and concerning this it is said
(שְׁמוֹת י"ט, ה'):
(Shemos 19:5):
וִהְיִיתֶם לִי סְגֻלָּה.
"And you shall be unto Me a treasured possession (segulah)."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is along the lines of what is said
(מַלְאָכִי א', ב'):
(Malachi 1:2):
הֲלוֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב... וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב.
"Was not Esav brother to Yaakov?... Yet I loved Yaakov."
וְאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהַמְכוּוָן אַף אִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם דּוֹמִים מַעֲשֵׂי יַעֲקֹב לְעֵשָׂו,
And we have explained that the meaning is: even if, God forbid, Yaakov's deeds resemble Esav's,
גַּם אִם עֵשָׂו מֵיטִיב מַעֲשָׂיו כְּיַעֲקֹב,
and even if Esav improves his deeds to appear like Yaakov
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לֶעָתִיד,
just as the idolaters will do in the future,
שֶׁזֶּה מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו לְרַמּוֹת וְלוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם הוּא טָהוֹר וְעוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹן עוֹשָׂיו,
for this is Esav's way, to deceive and claim that he too is pure and does the will of his Maker,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה עֵשָׂו לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁמִּתְעַטֵּף בְּטַלִּיתוֹ כְּזָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב
and as Esav will do in the World to Come, wrapping himself in his tallis like an elder and sitting beside Yaakov
(תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת צַו ב'),
(Tanchuma Parshas Tzav 2),
וְכֵן הָאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בּוֹחֲרִים לִפְנִים בְּמִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת מִתּוֹרָתֵינוּ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה וְאוֹמְרִים: אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
and similarly the nations of the world outwardly adopt good traits from our holy Torah and say, "We are Israel"
(תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תִשָּׂא ל"ד)
(Tanchuma Ki Sisa 34)
אַךְ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּן אֶת הַלְּבָבוֹת מֵעִיד שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְשׁוּרִים בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה:
nevertheless Hashem, may He be blessed, Who judges hearts, testifies that Israel are bound to the very root of primordial thought:
בְּרֵאשִׁית בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרָא רֵאשִׁית,
"Bereishis—for the sake of Israel, who are called Reishis (first),"
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: הֲלוֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב.
and concerning this it is said: "Was not Esav brother to Yaakov? And even so, I loved Yaakov."
וְזֶהוּ סְגוּלָּה בְּלֹא טַעַם,
And this is a segulah without rational reason,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְגֻלָּתוֹ,
and this is what is said: "Israel as His segulah,"
וְזֶה עַתִּיקָא, רְצוֹן הָרְצוֹנוֹת, מַאֲמָר בְּרֵאשִׁית.
and this is Atika, the Will of all wills, the utterance of Bereishis.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי זָכַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב פָּסוּק: כִּי יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ יָהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְגֻלָּתוֹ,
And therefore Rav Acha bar Yaakov cited the verse "For Yaakov did Kah choose for Himself, Israel as His segulah,"
שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל.
for on account of this it is called the Great Hallel.
וְחַג הַפֶּסַח לְכָל הַחֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת הוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And the festival of Pesach according to all reckonings corresponds to our father Avraham, peace be upon him,
וְאֵלָיו נִתְגַּלָּה גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
and to him were revealed the Egyptian exile and the Exodus from Egypt.
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת חֶסֶד וּגְדוּלָּה,
And our father Avraham is a chariot for the attribute of Chessed and Gedulah,
וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַחֶסֶד עַד עַתִּיקָא,
and the expansion of Chessed reaches up to Atika,
וְהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁזָּכָה לְמִדַּת זָקֵן, דִּכְתִיב
and he was the first to merit the attribute of "Zakein" (Elder), as it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ד, א'):
(Bereishis 24:1):
וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים,
"And Avraham was old, advanced in days,"
וּמְפָרֵשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and it is explained in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' קכ"ט.):
בְּיוֹמִין עִילָּאִין,
"into the supernal days"
וְהַיְינוּ בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדָּתוֹ עַד עַתִּיקָא
meaning into the first three Sefiros, for he was refined in his attribute all the way up to Atika
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים).
(as has been explained many times).
וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד הָיָה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And the Exodus from Egypt was through the attribute of Chessed, as is known.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת כָּלוּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו,
And we have already explained that in Shabbos is included the holiness of the festivals that will arrive in the weekdays following it,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים.
as we say: "And You sanctified it above all seasons."
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם חַג הַפֶּסַח שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל,
And for this reason the Shabbos before the festival of Pesach is called Shabbos HaGadol,
עַל שֵׁם גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים חַי בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
after "the Great One of the worlds, living in the heights of the universe."

paragraphs.text: Berachos 4b — "Whoever says Tehillah LeDavid (Tehillim 145) three times every day is assured of the World to Come. Why? If because it follows the Alef-Beis, let him say 'Ashrei temimei derech,' which has eight per letter. Rather, because it contains 'You open Your hand.' Then let him say the Great Hallel, which has 'He gives bread to all flesh'! Rather, because it has both." Rashi: it follows the Alef-Beis and contains the praise of providing food for all living things.

rich.text: Berachos 4b

— "Whoever says Tehillah LeDavid (Tehillim 145) three times every day is assured of the World to Come. Why? If because it follows the Alef-Beis, let him say 'Ashrei temimei derech,' which has eight per letter. Rather, because it contains 'You open Your hand.' Then let him say the Great Hallel, which has 'He gives bread to all flesh'! Rather, because it has both." Rashi: it follows the Alef-Beis and contains the praise of providing food for all living things.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 50 — “The aspect of Ayin is the mazal for Israel, the root of Atika, beyond comprehension, and from there comes the flow of sustenance. ‘Great’ denotes the utmost greatness, the aspect of Atik. And they said that a person's sustenance is as hard as the splitting of the Sea, for the splitting of the Sea too was beyond comprehension: there was the accusation, ‘How are these different from those?’, and the Zohar says, ‘On Atika the matter depends.’ So too sustenance: why this one and not that one depends only on mazal, the Ayin beyond comprehension.” Connection: The same identification of the mazal of sustenance with Atika and of "Gadol" with that height; it adds that sustenance and the splitting of the Sea rest alike on Atika, beyond the question of who deserves.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Gevuros Hashem 65 — “The point of saying that the Holy One, blessed is He, sits in the heights of the world is to make known that the Blessed One is the sustaining existence of all beings, and therefore He gives them existence and provides for them; and this is higher in rank than creation itself. So it says He sits in the heights of the world when He distributes sustenance, to teach of a greater level from which sustenance comes. Every created thing, by its very essence, is lacking and needs a cause to sustain it; sustenance is the very existence of the creature, and therefore sustenance stands higher than creation.” Connection: Maharal too reads the heights of the world as a source of sustenance above the order of creation; he gives the philosophical reason, that what sustains a lacking creature must stand above it, where Rav Tzadok names that source Atika, above the Name Havayah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Day of Pesach 8 — “Were it not that it contains two things, the Great Hallel, with ‘Who gives bread to all flesh,’ would truly rank above ‘You open Your hand.’ As my grandfather explained, the initials of ‘You open Your hand’ equal in gematria Havayah and Adonai, showing that the flow comes in graded order through man's service; but ‘Who gives bread to all flesh’ is still from the Holy One's kindness before man's service, like the twenty-six generations before the Giving of the Torah, who were nourished only by His kindness. Therefore ‘You open Your hand’ is arranged alphabetically, a flow descending in order, while the Great Hallel is not, a flow above the order.” Connection: The same question of why Hodu and not Ashrei is the Great Hallel; Sod Yesharim answers it through ordered, earned flow against flow above all order.
